relations.rationale: Taking a wrong turn suggests delay, but claim 12 says Jun still arrived before the group set off, indicating recovery from the mistake; not a strong logical push either way.
Jun's wrong turn has no bearing on Esme and Dara's team assignment.
Taking a wrong turn near the visitor center says nothing about Jun's age relative to others.
Jun's navigational error is unrelated to the number of teams.
Arriving before the group departed does not indicate anything about Jun's age.
Jun's timely arrival has no connection to Esme and Eli's team assignments.
The trail description and the stream stop are both parts of the same journey but neither confirms or denies the other; they are compatible but not directly supportive.
The trail leading through forest and meadow could plausibly lead toward a rocky outcrop reached by midday, forming a continuous narrative that mildly supports the timeline.
Esme and Dara being on different teams doesn't directly determine Dara and Eli's team relationship, since there could be more than two people involved.
Team assignment of Esme and Dara has no bearing on Jun's pace-setting behavior.
Esme and Dara being on different teams doesn't determine Esme and Eli's team relationship without knowing Dara and Eli's assignment.
If Esme and Dara are on different teams, this is consistent with there being two teams, supporting that claim.
Both describe stops during the same trek, forming a plausible sequential narrative, but neither logically necessitates the other.
Dara and Eli being on different teams doesn't directly imply anything about Esme and Eli without knowing Esme's team relative to Dara.
Dara and Eli being on different teams is consistent with and supports the existence of exactly two teams.
Jun being the oldest and Yara being the youngest are compatible claims that mutually support a consistent age ranking within the group.
Jun's being oldest doesn't causally relate to Yara's time-tracking behavior.
Jun setting the pace for the group has no bearing on how many teams exist.
Jun setting a steady pace and Yara tracking time toward sunset both suggest coordinated time management, but they don't directly imply each other.

Jun setting a steady pace throughout is a separate behavior from the group quickening pace due to clouds, though both concern pace; the earlier established norm doesn't necessarily support or contradict a later situational change.
